description: Task 1.4 — sidecar supervisor + secure IPC + single typed TS client + live engine status badge. Rust side (thin secure client + process manager, NO business logic): generate a per-session 256-bit bearer token, pick a FREE loopback ephemeral port, spawn the engine (dev: `python -m texora_engine`; prod: the frozen externalBin sidecar named with -$TARGET_TRIPLE), health-check GET /healthz, restart with exponential backoff on failure, expose a `engine_status()` Tauri command and emit `engine://status` events. TS side: a SINGLE typed client (apps/desktop/src/engineClient.ts) is the only place that calls invoke/listen/fetch; a live status badge on the Home screen consumes it, with all strings via i18next (id default + en). Depends on FEAT-M1C-002 (Tauri app must build first). done: (tasks.md 1.4) 'UI shows live engine status from /healthz' — verified structurally + unit tests; the running-window observation is manual.
steps: Read context.json and m1-continue-plan.md (Item 2) FIRST. Apply the PATH export. cwd for cargo = apps/desktop/src-tauri; cwd for frontend/git = worktree root. Also read engine/texora_engine/__main__.py (the dev-spawn CLI contract) and design.md section 1.1 (process lifecycle) before writing the supervisor.

Add pinned Rust deps to apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml: tokio (features rt-multi-thread, process, time, macros), rand 0.8, ureq 2.x (chosen loopback HTTP health-check client — run blocking calls on a blocking task), and tauri-plugin-shell 2.x (official sidecar spawn so externalBin -$TARGET_TRIPLE resolution is handled by Tauri). Verify exact current versions against crates.io before pinning.

Create apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/supervisor.rs: pure, unit-testable helpers `free_loopback_port()` (bind 127.0.0.1:0, read the assigned port, drop the listener), a 256-bit token generator (hex/base64, non-empty, unique per call), and a backoff schedule (increasing, capped); plus the spawn + health-check loop + status broadcast. DEV mode runs the venv module `python -m texora_engine --host 127.0.0.1 --port

--token ` passing the token via the TEXORA_ENGINE_TOKEN env to avoid argv leakage; PROD mode launches the externalBin sidecar texora-engine. Emit `engine://status` on every state change. Never spawn a real long-running engine inside unit tests.

Wire the supervisor in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs: register tauri-plugin-shell, start the supervisor on setup into managed state, expose `#[tauri::command] engine_status()` returning the typed status, and keep main.rs unchanged. Add the required permissions to apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json (the engine_status command, the engine://status event, and a shell sidecar scope limited to binaries/texora-engine). Keep ALL business logic out of Rust.

Create the single typed client apps/desktop/src/engineClient.ts: export an `EngineStatus` type (e.g. { state: 'starting'|'healthy'|'unhealthy'|'restarting'|'stopped'; port?: number; detail?: string }), `getEngineStatus()` wrapping invoke('engine_status'), and `subscribeEngineStatus(cb)` wrapping listen('engine://status'). This module is the ONLY place that imports @tauri-apps/api invoke/event. Add @tauri-apps/plugin-shell (JS) to match the Rust plugin.

Add i18next: apps/desktop/src/i18n.ts + apps/desktop/src/locales/{id,en}.json initialized in main.tsx with id as default language (coding-standards forbids hard-coded UI text; 1.4's badge needs real strings). Create apps/desktop/src/EngineStatusBadge.tsx that renders the live status from engineClient with i18next strings, and render <EngineStatusBadge /> from apps/desktop/src/App.tsx.

Add tests: Rust `cargo test` unit tests in supervisor.rs (free_loopback_port returns a usable port, token is non-empty/256-bit/unique, backoff increases and caps); frontend apps/desktop/src/engineClient.test.ts and a badge render test (mock @tauri-apps/api invoke + event; drive through engine_status and engine://status). Keep existing App tests green.

Update docs/LICENSES.md in THIS change: add rows for tokio, rand, ureq, tauri-plugin-shell (crates.io) and i18next, react-i18next, @tauri-apps/plugin-shell (npm); REMOVE the reqwest candidate row (ureq is the chosen client) and the note pairing them. Verify each license against official metadata before writing the row.

Run the full verification (below), append real output + outcomes to docs/m1-verification.md §1.4 noting that live-status-in-a-running-window is pending MANUAL confirmation, set this FEAT status to completed, record findings, and commit locally e.g. `feat(desktop): sidecar supervisor + typed engine client + live status badge (task 1.4)`. Do NOT push/merge.
acceptance_criteria: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/supervisor.rs exists with unit-tested free_loopback_port, 256-bit token generation, and capped backoff; lib.rs exposes engine_status() and emits engine://status; capabilities/default.json grants exactly the needed permissions with the sidecar scoped to binaries/texora-engine.
apps/desktop/src/engineClient.ts is the only module importing @tauri-apps/api invoke/event; EngineStatusBadge renders live status via i18next (id+en) and is shown on the Home screen.

findings:
Completed. Rust supervisor (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/supervisor.rs) implements the 256-bit hex session token (rand::rngs::OsRng), free_loopback_port() (bind 127.0.0.1:0 -> read -> drop), capped exponential BackoffSchedule, dev/prod engine spawn via tauri-plugin-shell (dev: python -m texora_engine; prod: texora-engine externalBin), ureq /healthz polling on blocking tasks, and engine://status broadcasts. lib.rs registers the shell plugin, manages SupervisorState, starts the supervisor on setup, and exposes #[tauri::command] engine_status(); main.rs unchanged. capabilities/default.json grants core:default + shell:allow-execute scoped to binaries/texora-engine. Business logic stays out of Rust.

TS: src/engineClient.ts is the ONLY production module importing invoke/listen (grep-confirmed); exports EngineStatus, getEngineStatus(), subscribeEngineStatus(). i18n added (src/i18n.ts + locales/{id,en}.json, id default + en fallback, initialized in main.tsx); src/EngineStatusBadge.tsx renders live status via i18next and is shown on Home (App.tsx). App.tsx strings routed through i18next. Added resolveJsonModule:true to tsconfig.json for the locale JSON imports.

Deps pinned + versions/licenses verified against official sources and added to docs/LICENSES.md in this change: crates tokio 1.53.3 (MIT), rand 0.8.8 (MIT OR Apache-2.0), ureq 2.12.1 (MIT OR Apache-2.0), tauri-plugin-shell 2.5.0 (MIT OR Apache-2.0); npm i18next 26.4.7 (MIT), react-i18next 17.0.20 (MIT), @tauri-apps/plugin-shell 2.5.0 (Apache-2.0 OR MIT). The reqwest candidate row and the reqwest/ureq pairing note were removed; ureq is the sole health-check client. rand pinned to 0.8.8 per plan (0.10 exists but the plan pins 0.8.x for API stability); ureq pinned to 2.x (3.x has a different http-crate API, out of plan scope).

Verification (all PASS): cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test (7 supervisor unit tests: port/token/backoff/serde), cargo build; pnpm --filter desktop lint, test -- --run (6 tests across App + engineClient + EngineStatusBadge), build. Evidence appended to docs/m1-verification.md Section 1.4.

FINDING (host, in-scope note): the MSVC toolchain the Section 1.2 log reported as ABSENT is now present (VS 2022 Build Tools MSVC 14.44.35207 + Windows 10 SDK 10.0.26100.0). cargo only needed the MSVC env (LIB/INCLUDE/PATH) loaded via vcvars64.bat before running (bash does not inherit it); the prior LNK1181 dbghelp.lib failure was the SDK lib dir missing from LIB. All cargo checks were run inside a cmd session that calls vcvars64.bat first (via a throwaway wrapper that was deleted, not committed). This clears the Section 1.2 cargo-pending caveat at the local level.
